title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier‑Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM‑guided repair loop (Generate–Verify‑Repair, GVR) reduces verifier‑detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device‑configuration translation. Design: a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), requested generator gpt‑5‑mini, and a pybatfish‑style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared‑initial‑candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) with at most one bounded repair attempt per task. Outcomes (artifact‑backed): every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic validator in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution issues in the archive materially constrain inference: (1) executed shared‑generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per‑condition generation; (2) the prespecified comparison GVR vs schema‑constrained baseline (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier‑detectable benefit in this specific, artifact‑grounded setting because there were no verifier‑detectable errors to correct; results do not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, repair budget, or verifier. We provide artifact‑grounded recommendations to restore discordance potential and to evaluate GVR under adversarial, multi‑model, and expanded‑oracle regimes.

sections.introduction: LLM‑assisted intent→configuration translation promises operator productivity gains but risks producing syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect configurations that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow ordering, ACL/policy predicates). Prior work therefore recommends interposing deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before execution. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to ask a focused operational question: does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM‑guided repair loop reduce verifier‑detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline, under a frozen, archived design? The run and all analytic artifacts are archived (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d). Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks) using gpt‑5‑mini and a deterministic pybatfish‑style validator; (2) transparent execution accounting showing shared‑initial‑candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240) and that every generation satisfied the validator (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null and an explicit reconciliation of the preregistered power assumptions and executed semantics; and (4) operational recommendations grounded in the archived evidence.
sections.related_work: Three literatures motivate and contextualize the study. (i) LLM failure analyses and surveys document hallucinations and fabricated outputs for code and structured artifacts, motivating validator‑interposed pipelines for safety (see archived evidence_synthesis C1, C3, and cited surveys). (ii) Generate–verify–repair and constrained‑decoding architectures improve mechanically checkable properties (compilation, grammar validity) in prior work; case studies report reduced surface failures but leave semantic correctness on domain invariants an open question (evidence_synthesis C2). (iii) NetOps research emphasizes verifier‑driven evaluation (reachability, policy invariants) and human oversight for high‑stakes changes. Our run differs by being preregistered, paired, and artifact‑archived; it therefore supplies a deterministic accounting of execution semantics and their inferential consequences that complements prior benchmark and prototype reports.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: Preregistered study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in verifier‑detected violation rate). Two prespecified primary comparisons were listed: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema‑constrained decoding with Bonferroni correction (family α = 0.05). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 (frozen). Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks). Requested generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial executed semantics (recorded in the manifest): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); maximum_model_calls budget = 480. Execution accounting: execution_manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 240. Task bank and oracle: public synthetic NetOps task bank encodes initial device states, intent, workflow constraints, and expected final states; scoring rule = full_intent_constraint_validation implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Missingness and exclusions: preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness rules were applied; analysis artifacts show zero failed episodes and zero exclusions.
sections.results: Execution artifacts (authoritative): model_calls_used = 240 under shared‑initial_candidate semantics; complete_pair_count = 240. Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Statistical outputs from the preregistered executor: exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired‑bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; resamples = 10,000; bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Repair diagnostics: for every episode validator_trace.repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate already satisfied validator predicates for all tasks (representative per‑task scoring artifacts archived under execution/scoring/). Contamination and missingness artifacts (analysis/contamination_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) report zero flags and zero failures. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm episode and provider‑call accounting and that all deterministic consistency checks passed.
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation and degeneracy: zero discordant pairs make the paired McNemar test and bootstrap CI degenerate: with n10 = n01 = 0 there is no within‑pair disagreement to estimate an effect, so p = 1.00 and CI = [0.0,0.0] are deterministic consequences under the preregistered analysis executor. The degeneracy traces to executed shared‑initial_candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), which eliminated stochastic variation between arms and hence removed the discordance GVR could exploit. This execution‑vs‑preregistration mismatch invalidates the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per‑condition generation (explicit preregistration vs executed semantic deviation recorded in the archive). Procedural deviation: the prespecified schema‑constrained baseline comparison (C vs B) listed in the preregistration was not executed; archived artifacts record no rationale for that omission. Threats to validity: internal validity is compromised by the preregistration→execution mismatch; construct validity is limited by verifier completeness (passing the deterministic validator does not guarantee absence of all operational risks); external validity is constrained by a single generator (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, a one‑attempt repair budget, and a single verifier; conclusion validity is limited because zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. Operational recommendations (artifact‑grounded): (1) re‑run using independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) to restore discordance potential; archived task manifest and RNG seeds permit deterministic reruns; (2) inject adversarial/golden tasks (preregistered plan included 10% golden injections) to validate verifier sensitivity; (3) expand model scope beyond gpt‑5‑mini and increase repair budget/iterations to observe repair dynamics; (4) broaden verifier invariants or integrate formal verification hybrids to reduce oracle incompleteness; (5) always report generation semantics and model_calls_used (the archive shows model_calls_used = 240 vs maximum_model_calls = 480). Relation to prior work: the null outcome under shared generation aligns with the literature’s emphasis that measurable GVR benefit depends on evaluation semantics, verifier coverage, and generator stochasticity—i.e., verification pipelines can only reduce the errors the verifier can detect and only when there is discordance for repair to resolve.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Under the executed shared‑initial_candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), yielding a degenerate null estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR added no verifier‑detectable value in this exact, artifact‑grounded setting because no verifier‑detectable errors were present to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference and are explicitly recorded in the archive: (1) shared‑generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent‑generation power assumption, and (2) the prespecified C vs B comparison was not executed. We release the authoritative artifacts so others can reproduce the accounting and run the preregistered independent‑generation and adversarial experiments needed to robustly assess GVR’s operational value under conditions that restore discordance potential and verifier sensitivity.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish‑style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor‑specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared‑generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design removed per‑arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per‑condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per‑condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single‑model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt‑5‑mini); cross‑model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema‑constrained‑baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
